column1: # Where every agent skill comes from. One row per skill, TSV, '# ' comments.
#           spec = GitHub repository that owns the skill. Linked from a checkout
#           when one exists (so it updates with `git pull`), otherwise fetched
#           with `npx skills add <repo> --skill <id> -g`. The CLI does not
#           discover every layout, so a clone is the reliable path.
#   dagr    owned by the herdr-dagr plugin. Extracted with `dagr --skill` into
#           that plugin's own skills/ directory (next to its examples/), then
#           linked. spec = herdr plugin id that provides the dagr binary.
#   bundle  no installable home exists, so this repo is the source of truth.
#           spec = path in this repo. This is debt: the `why` says what would
#           let it be deleted, and scripts/skills-sync.sh reports the count.

column4: This repo's own install/configure/upgrade guide; home is this repo by definition.
Apothic-AI/one-shot-genius exists but is empty (0 bytes, no commits), so `npx skills add` cannot fetch it yet. Becomes kind=repo once the skill is pushed.

Fork of the skill `herdr --skill` ships: ~56 delta lines, mostly target-verification-before-delegation, which this orchestration setup depends on. Rebase onto the shipped file when herdr changes and send the delta upstream; becomes kind=shipped when herdr takes it.

Owned by the herdr-dagr plugin pinned in herdr/plugins.toml. Never bundle: `dagr --skill` is byte-identical to the plugin's own copy, so a bundled copy is a silent fork of a file the plugin already owns.
Owned by our fork, which ships skills/unblock/SKILL.md. The fork's copy is newer than any bundled copy (it documents queue-page sign-in), so bundling would freeze agents on a stale skill.
